content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_nine>
Required: 9 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_states_eight_plus>
Backend engineering: 8+ years building transactional services, most
recently a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day.
</document>

Assess the candidate summary above against the posting requirement and say
whether the candidate matches it.

Report the match as it actually is. Where the summary cannot establish the
requirement, say so rather than assuming either way.

response.text:
**Match status: Cannot be established from the summary.**

- **Requirement** (DOC_req_years_nine): 9 years of backend engineering experience.
- **Candidate** (DOC_summary_states_eight_plus): "8+ years" of backend engineering.

"8+" sets a floor of 8 years but no ceiling. The candidate could have anywhere from 8 years (one short) to 9 or more (meets it). The summary supports neither "meets" nor "does not meet."

**What the summary does establish:**
- At least 8 years in the relevant field (backend/transactional services), which is within a year of the requirement.
- Recent, relevant, production-scale work: a settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. This speaks to the kind of experience, not its length.

**To resolve it:** Ask the candidate for their exact years of backend experience, or check dated employment history on the full résumé. If the 9-year requirement is strict, this needs to be confirmed before treating the candidate as qualified.
